insight.title: Why You Choose the Easiest Idea Instead of the Best One
insight.subtitle: How seeking certainty stops you from finding a real breakthrough

sections.text: Your brain treats "innovative" and "unpredictable" as the same threat. To stay safe, it often discards the most creative solution simply because it cannot visualize the exact outcome, favoring mediocrity over unknown potential.

Behavioral psychology shows we suffer from "ambiguity aversion." We prefer a small, guaranteed reward over a potentially massive one if the path is unclear. In decision-making, clarity is often mistaken for quality.
When choosing a strategy, you likely lean toward the one that feels "polished." But innovation lives in the mess. If a plan feels too comfortable, it is probably because you have seen it before.
Try this today: The next time you make a choice today, ask which option feels the most uncertain.
Clarity is a sign of a finished thought, but uncertainty is the signal of a new one.
